observed_title: Selections of Integrable Multifunctions in Arbitrary Banach Spaces

read_ranges.scope: 逐页阅读全文：多值Pettis、Henstock–Kurzweil–Pettis、Henstock/McShane/Birkhoff与variationally Henstock章节、证明草图、参考文献。

topic_relevance.M04: direct for measurable/scalarly measurable selections from measurable multifunctions and integrability-preserving conditions, including arbitrary (possibly nonseparable) Banach ranges. It does not establish measurable argmax selection, analytic projection measurability, or legality of a selector constrained by an optimization objective; its results are reusable only where the target correspondence meets its scalar-measurability, weak-compactness, and integrability assumptions.

definitions.name: Scalar measurability
definitions.statement: For every x*∈X*, the support function s(x*,Γ(·))=sup_{x∈Γ(·)}<x*,x> is measurable. The chapter distinguishes this from Effros measurability of the correspondence and Bochner measurability.

definitions.name: cwk(X)-valued multifunction
definitions.statement: Γ takes nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of a Banach space X.

definitions.name: Pettis multivalued integrability
definitions.statement: Each support function s(x*,Γ(·)) is Lebesgue-integrable and for every measurable set A there is MΓ(A)∈cwk(X) whose support function is the integral of s(x*,Γ(·)) on A.

definitions.name: Aumann integral
definitions.statement: The set of integrals of L1 selections of a measurable multifunction; it may be empty if no integrable selection exists.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem A / Theorem B: characterization of Pettis-integrable multifunctions by selections
assumptions: Γ:Ω→cwk(X) on a complete finite measure space.
For Theorem A, X is separable; for Theorem B, X is arbitrary and Γ is scalar measurable.
theorem_cards.statement: In a separable Banach space, Γ is Pettis integrable iff the support-function family {s(x*,Γ(·)):x*∈B_X*} is uniformly integrable and all scalar-measurable selections are Pettis integrable. In an arbitrary Banach space, the cited Theorem B gives Pettis integrability iff all scalar-measurable selections are Pettis integrable, and Pettis integrability implies the support-function family is uniformly integrable. The chapter also states that scalar-measurable selections exist for scalar-measurable weakly compact-valued multifunctions, citing Cascales–Kadets–Rodríguez.
proof_steps: These are reported as results from prior papers; the chapter supplies no proof of Theorem A/B.

The chapter emphasizes that equality between the multivalued Pettis integral and the set of Pettis integrals of selections generally fails in a nonseparable Banach space, even though the family is nonempty (formula (3), lines 247–252).
gaps: The equivalence and selector existence rely on cited external theorems; the source is a survey/chapter, not a primary proof.
These theorems concern integrability, not maximization or argmax selection.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.3: HKP integrability and scalar-measurable selections
assumptions: Γ:[0,1]→cwk(X) is scalar measurable, X any Banach space.
theorem_cards.statement: Γ is Henstock–Kurzweil–Pettis integrable iff every scalar-measurable selection of Γ is Henstock integrable; the HKP multivalued integral equals the set of integrals of its HKP-integrable selections on each interval.
proof_steps: In the forward direction, bound each selected scalar projection between −s(−x*,Γ) and s(x*,Γ); use support-function integrability and the weakly compact integral values to obtain HKP integrability.
For the reverse direction, for fixed x*, form the exposed face G(t)={x∈Γ(t):<x*,x>=s(x*,Γ(t))}; cited measurable-selection results provide a scalar-measurable selector g of G.
That selector attains the support-function integral and hence identifies the support function of the closure/convex set of selection integrals; James weak compactness yields the desired cwk(X) value.
gaps: Proof is explicitly a sketch and invokes prior measurable-selection results and James characterization.
This uses a fixed linear functional exposed face, not a measurable selector of maximizers over a general parameterized optimization problem.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 5.4 and Theorem 6.6: selection plus integrability decomposition
assumptions: Theorem 6.6: Γ is variationally Henstock integrable, X any Banach space.
theorem_cards.statement: Theorem 5.4 characterizes Henstock integrability by existence of a Henstock-integrable selector f such that Γ−f is McShane integrable (with the stated quantification over such selectors). Theorem 6.6 states that a variationally Henstock integrable Γ has a nonempty family of variationally Henstock-integrable selections and, moreover, every strongly measurable selection is variationally Henstock integrable.
proof_steps: Theorem 5.4 is quoted from [12] without proof.

Theorem 6.6 proof uses variational Henstock measurability to get Bochner measurability/strongly measurable selectors, subtracts a chosen selector to form a Pettis-integrable residual multifunction, and uses absolute continuity of the variation measure plus the Radström embedding to transfer variational Henstock integrability.
gaps: Theorem 5.4 is a cited result and the proof of Theorem 6.6 relies on cited propositions/theorems about measurability, Pettis integrability, and Radström embedding.
These are integration/selection results; no measurable optimization objective, analytic projection, or argmax map is treated.

constant_dependence.explicit: No quantitative selector modulus is asserted. Selection existence/integrability is conditional on scalar measurability, cwk(X) values and the corresponding integrability hypotheses; the source does not provide finite-dimensional measurable-selection error bounds.

endpoint_limits.scope: Complete finite measure spaces; weakly compact convex-valued multifunctions; arbitrary Banach target in the cited scalar-measurability results. Integrability notions vary by section (Pettis/HKP/gauge/variational).
endpoint_limits.not_established: No theorem identifies measurable selectors with optimizers, proves Borel/analytic selector under arbitrary graph assumptions, or handles nonattainment of a pointwise supremum.

reusable_methods.method: Use support functions to define scalar measurability and encode the set-valued integral.
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires a weakly compact convex-valued correspondence; it is not by itself a measurable argmax construction.

reusable_methods.method: For a fixed x*, pass to the exposed-face correspondence {x∈Γ(t):<x*,x>=s(x*,Γ(t))} and select a point attaining the support function.
reusable_methods.transfer: This realizes a linear support supremum when the cited face-measurability and selection assumptions apply; general objective families need separate joint measurability/graph hypotheses.

reusable_methods.method: Subtract an integrable selector to decompose a multifunction into a selected part plus an integrable residual.
reusable_methods.transfer: Useful for integration-compatible selector interfaces, not for proving a measurable optimizer exists.

unchecked: All source pages were read; stated results from cited papers were not independently checked against their original proofs.
This source supports a measurable-selection method family, but the chapter does not prove the M04 analytic-projection or measurable-argmax claims.
